Built against [wamsoft/krkrz_dev](https://github.com/wamsoft/krkrz_dev) V2.6.5

- **The game's own mouse pointers**: the arrow, over buttons, at a click wait, in auto mode, over a text field, over something to drag, busy, drawn in the game's colours and at the same size on the screen however the window zooms the game. Config's Mouse Pointer picks the game's or the system's. Desktops and the browser
- **Where a question puts the pointer**: a Yes/No prompt no longer moves the pointer to No by itself; Config's Pointer on Questions leaves it where it is, or puts it on No or on Yes
- **Saves that outlast a patch**: a save made before an update of its script goes on from the line it was made at, wherever added or removed lines have moved it, and its backlog with it; up to 0.26.1 any change to a script sent its saves back to the top of their scene
- **Advanced settings**: Help > Show Advanced Settings adds an Advanced menu, and the manual has a page of them on every platform: memory use, the picture cache, the drawing threads, the controller and the movies' size, each taking effect at once
- For game makers: kagex-release keeps a CG that differs a little from the one before it (a face, an arm) as the rectangle that differs (`media.images.cgPieces`, `evimage` by default; `cgpieces.txt`, drawn back by the framework), measures every sound's loudness and brings voices, music or sound effects to targets (`loudness.measure`, `loudness.targets`, `--cli loudness`), and puts a game's own Android plugins (`plugins/android/<ABI>/`) in the APK; the README has notes for plugin authors; a compile logs how many lines of each scene are new and gone since the last; `cursors.csv` (`GameCursor.tjs`); `changeUserConf` (`Advanced.tjs`)
- kagex-release 0.27.0 downloads the 0.27.0 engines

The sample game with Live2D (`kagex_sample_live2d_<platform>`, added to this release once it's out) holds Live2D's Cubism Core: by installing or playing it you agree not to copy the Cubism Core out of it, distribute it apart from the game, modify it, or reverse engineer, decompile or disassemble it. It uses sample data owned and copyrighted by Live2D Inc.

Everything in this release is listed in [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/krkren/kagex/blob/0.27.0/CHANGELOG.md).

On Windows the engine needs OpenGL ES: a graphics driver that supports it, or ANGLE's `libEGL.dll` and `libGLESv2.dll` next to `krkrz.exe`.

The macOS app and tools aren't signed with an Apple Developer ID, so macOS blocks them the first time: open the app from the context menu (Open), or allow it under System Settings > Privacy & Security; for the tools, `xattr -d com.apple.quarantine kagex-release kagex-lipsync`. The Android APK is signed with a debug key: allow installs from unknown sources, or use `adb install`. The sample's iOS build is for the Simulator; kagex-release signs a game for iPhones and iPads with your own Apple Developer certificate.
